summary: Rice simmered in a large excess of water until the grains break down. Used here as a worked example of a record whose variants differ by ratio and finishing rather than by ingredient list.

variants.label: Thin, long simmer
variants.difference_note: Roughly one part rice to twelve parts water, simmered until the grains lose their edges and the liquid turns opaque.

variants.label: Thick, short simmer
variants.difference_note: Roughly one part rice to eight parts water and a shorter cook, leaving whole grains suspended in the liquid. Kept as its own variant, not treated as an undercooked version of the first.

ingredients.note: Choose the ratio from the variant you are following.
Added at the end, since the liquid reduces while cooking.

ingredients.item: Fresh spring onion, ginger, or a spoon of oil
ingredients.note: Finishing only; not part of the base preparation.

method.instruction: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water running off is no longer cloudy, then drain.
Combine the rice and the full quantity of water in a heavy pot and bring to a boil over high heat.
Lower the heat until the surface is barely moving and set the lid slightly ajar so the pot does not boil over.
Simmer, stirring every ten minutes or so to keep the rice from catching on the base: about 40 minutes for the thin variant, about 25 for the thick one.
Stop when the texture matches the variant you are following. The porridge continues to thicken as it cools, so pull it slightly looser than you want it.
Season with salt off the heat, and add any finishing ingredients just before serving.

caveats: Starchy porridge boils over easily and the foam that escapes is scalding; keep the lid ajar and the heat low.
This record has had no food-safety review. Treat it as an interface fixture, not as kitchen guidance.
